key_insight: VisDom tackles sparse novel view synthesis by adding a visible-domain constraint that better limits geometry to what is actually observable from the input views. This helps reduce floating artifacts and improves consistency when training NeRF- or Gaussian Splatting-based models with very few images.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the instability of novel view synthesis in sparse-view settings, where limited supervision makes it hard to recover accurate 3D geometry and leads to overfitting, floating artifacts, and silhouette-consistent but incorrect shapes.
method: Introduces a visible-domain constraint to restrict learned geometry to regions supported by the observed views.
Uses this constraint as a regularizer alongside standard sparse-view training to reduce hallucinated structure.
Targets both NeRF- and Gaussian Splatting-based pipelines to improve robustness under sparse supervision.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, VisDom offers a practical way to make sparse-view 3D reconstruction more reliable without requiring many additional input images. It can improve visual quality and geometric consistency in real-world applications where dense capture is expensive or impossible.
